caseno: Memorandum of Appeal from Original Decree (FA) No. 55 of 1980.
lawyer:
Fazlul Karim with Abu Bakar Siddique and Mushod R. Sobban, Advoctes—For the Appellant. 
Abdul Baset Majumder with Rabi Sankar Chokraberty and Md Enamul Huq, Advocates—For the Respondents.
parties:
Nurul Islam Chowdhury ------ Petitioner
vs
Mvi Fazal Ahmed being dead his heirs 1(1) Morshedul Alam and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the suit land measuring 17 drones 5 kanis 1 gonda and 1 kara as described in schedules to the plaintiff originally belonged to Fazal Karim Khan, who possessed the same in khas. While being the rightful owner-in-possession Fazal Kabir settled 14 drones of the land with Md Putan by a registered patta dated 2nd Falgoon, 1308 BS and since than he owned and possessed the same. The said suit land was, of course, acquired by Putan in the benami of his son Ali Hossain on 1-2-1901 but he was the real ostensible owner of the land as it was acquired with his own money and for his own benefit. After taking settlement Md Putan possessed the suit land in khas on payment of rent to the landlords. After some time landlord Fazal . Khan forcibly dispossessed Mr Putan from the said land whereupon Md Putan filed. TS No. 111 of 1906 against the said Fazal Kabir Khan for recovery of khas possession in the said 14 drones of lands out of the suit land on declaration of his title thereto and the said suit was eventually decreed on contest on 18-3-1907. Against the aforesaid Judgment and decree Fazal Kabir Khan filed Title Appeal No. 161 of 1911 but the said appeal was allowed due to formal defects in the plaint. Ali Hossain, a son and benamder of Md Putan for the aforesaid 14 droned of lands out of the suit land was added as a pro-forma defendant in the aforesaid Title Suit No. 89 of 1909. During the pendency of the aforesaid Title Appeal No. 161 of 1911 Fazal Kabir Khan transferred his superior interest in the aforesaid 14 drones of lands and khas interest in 3 drones 5 kanis 1 gonda and 1 kara of lands out of the suit land to his wife Ruh Afza alias Alimannessa by a registered deed of gift acted 18th Magh, 1316. BS. In this way the right, title, interest and possession of Md Putan in the 14 drones of lands were clearly established. Subsequently, the aforesaid Ruh Afza alias Alimannessa transferred her superior interest in the 14 drones of lands and khas interest in 3 drones 5 kanis 1 gonda and 1 kara of land out of the suit land to Md Putan by a registered kabala dated 10-6-1912, corresponding to 26th Baishak 1319 BS on receipt of proper consideration and he duly delivered possession thereof to Md Putan. In this way Md Putan owned and passed the entire suit land by way of settlement from Fazal Kabir Khan and by way of purchase by registered kabala from his wife Ruh Afza alias Alimannessa. In course of time, Md Putan executed a power of attorney in favour of his eldest son Ali Hossain for management of the suit property for its proper management and administration as he was unable to look after it properly due to his old age. Thereafter Ali Hossain kot mortgaged the suit property with one Sultan Ahmed Bahaddar on behalf of his father Mr Putan, on the strength of the said power of attorney, in order to save the suit property from auction sale for arrears of land revenue. Subsequently, Md Putan died in 1919 leaving Ali Hossain, Omar Ali, Ali Akbar, the predecessor of plaintiffs, Nos. 1-3 and defendant Nos. 1-6, 8-10 and 12-19, 20 and 30 as 3 sons and Khatijan, Johra and Fatema, the predecessor of plaintiff Nos. 4-15 and defendant No. 7 and 1 as 3 daughters as. his heirs and heiresses. In this way, each son of Md Putan acquired 2/9 share and each daughter of Md Putan acquired 1/9 share in the suit property. Then Khadeja died leaving Ejahar Meah and the predecessor of plaintiff Nos. 11-15, as two sons to succeed her. Thereafter Johara died leaving plaintiff Nos. 6-10 and defendant No. 7 as her heirs. Then Fatema died leaving plaintiffs Nos. 4-5 as her heirs. Thus the plaintiffs have calmed right, title and interest in 6 drones 6 kanis and 19 gondas of land out of the suit land by inheritance from Ali Akbar, son of Md Putan and Khadeja, Johara and Fatema, the 3 daughters of Md Putan, Omar Ali, son of Md Putan died leaving defendant No. 8 as son and defendant Nos. 9-10 and 12 and one Mahmuda Khatun as 4 daughters to succeed him. Thereafter, Mahmuda Khatun died leaving defendant Nos. 13-14 as heirs. Ali Hossain died leaving defendant Nos. 15-17 as 3 sons and defendant Nos. 18, 20, and 30 as 3 daughters and Pear Jan as wife. Defendant No. 31 has acquired the share of Pear Jan in the suit land by purchase by a registered kabala. Defendant No. 32 acquired the share of defendant No. 20 in the suit land by, purchase. Ali Akbar died leaving plaintiff Nos. 1-3 and defendant Nos. 1-6 to succeed him. After the death of Md Putan one Makbul Ali created a fraudulent and collusive kabala in respect of the suit land from Fazal Kabir Khan. Thereafter one Elahadad Chowdhury, father of defendant No. 27 and the brother''s son of said Makbul Ali acquired the kot mortgage interest in the suit land from Sultan Ahmed Bahaddar by a registered kabala dated 11-9-1924 corresponding to 26th Jaistha 1286. BS on payment of proper consideration and he possessed the suit land in khas as the mortgagee under the heirs and heiresses.of Md Putan through Sultan Ahmed Bahaddar. Makbul Ali acquired no right, title and interest in his suit land by his alleged kabala from Fazal Kabir Khan, who had already transferred his right, title and interest in the suit land to his wife Ruh Afza by a registered deed of gift and the said Ruh Afza in her turn, transferred her right, title and interest in the suit land to Md Putan. Ali though Md Putan became the absolute owner of 14 drones of land, the names of his heirs and heiresses were not recorded in the RS Khatian due to sheer inadvertent mistake. The RS record was prepared in the names of Ali Hossain and Elahadad Chowdhury as the mortgagees. The RS Record is evidently wrong and it is not binding upon the plaintiffs. As the aforesaid Elahadad Chowdhury being in possession of the suit property on the basis of purchase of the kot mortgage interest of Sultan Ahmed Bahaddar by registered kabalas, failed to pay rent for the suit land to the landlords the suit property was put to auction sale for arrears of rent and the said Elahadad Chowdhury fraudulently auction purchased the suit property in the benami of his uncle Jinnat Ali on 20-5-1931. Thereafter the said Elahadad Chowdhury created a collusive deed of relinquishment in his favour for the suit land in collusion with his uncle Makbul Ali and Jinnat Ali and, as such, Elahadad Chowdhury acquired no right, title and interest in the suit property. Elahabad Chowdhury then created a fraudulent, collusive and void deed of partition in respect of the suit property with some heirs of Ali Hossain on 25-2-1940 following which one of the heirs of Ali Hossain filed CS No. 13 of 1951 against the heirs of Ali Hossain and Elahadad Chowdhury for redemption of mortgage of the suit property and the said suit was eventually decreed on compromise in terms of a solenama filed by the heirs of late Elahadad Chowdhury and defendant Nos. 15-18 in the suit but the plaintiffs were not made parties in the aforesaid suit. The plaintiffs after coming to know about the said decree in OS No. 13 of 1951 demanded their shares in suit property from the heirs of Elahadad Chowdhury, following which the heirs of Ellahabad Chowdhury delivered to them possession in 5 drones of land, as described in schedules "Ka" to the plaint, out of the suit land amicably during the middle part of Baishak, 1955. In this way the plaintiffs have been possessing the ''Ka'' schedule lands in khas since Baishak, 1955 by amicable arrangement with the defendants without any partition by metes and bounds. The plaintiffs acquired right, title and interest in 6 drones 6 gandas of lands out of the suit land by inheritance from one son and 3 daughters of Md Putan to whom the suit land formerly belonged. Thereafter the other heirs to Ali Hossain. filed OS No. 35 of 1954 for cancellation of the solenama and the decree passed in OS No. 13 of 1961 against the heirs of Elahadad Chowdhury and others but the said suit was eventually dismissed. Thereafter the plaintiffs filed partition suit No. 16 of 1958 for partition of their shares which ultimately abated as some heirs to the deceased defendants were not brought on record in time. Under these circumstances, the plaintiffs have been constrained to file this suit for partition for a saham of 6 drones 6 kanis and 19 gondas of lands out of the suit land. 

 4. Defendant No. 21 who is the present appellant, also contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations of the plaint and contended, inter alia, that Md Putan and his sons Ali Hossain and Ali Akbar acquired 14 drones of lands out of the suit land recorded under CS Khatian No. 217 and RS Khatian No. 2 by way of settlement from Fazal Karim Khan in Dar Jote right and possessed the same in khas and then transferred 9 drones and 4 kanis of lands out of the said 14 drones of land to one Tripura Chowdhury and Prasanna Chowdhury by kot mortgage on receipt of Taka 4000.00 as mortgage money delivered possession of the said property to them. Thereafter the said Putan and his sons Ali Hossain and Ali Akbar transferred 4 drones and 12 kanis of land out of their 14 drones of land to one Surendra Chowdhury by a kot mortgage on receipt to Tk. 600.00 as mortgage money and delivered possession thereof to him. Thereafter Md Putan, Ali Akbar and Ali Hossain purchased the superior jote right in the said 14 drones of land and other khas lands of the jote. Thereafter Tripura Chowdhury and Prasanna Chowdhury filed mortgage suit No. 65 of 1921 for realisation, of the mortgage money against Ali Hossain, Ali Akbar and other heirs to Md Putan, which was decreed in preliminary form and one Jinnat Ali purchased the decree of Mortgage suit No. 65 of 1921 from Tripura and Prasanna Chowdhury subsequently. Jinnat Ali put the said 9 drones and 4 kanis of land to auction sale which, was purchased by Jinnat Ali himself, and he got into possession in the suit lands on obtaining sale certificate and delivery of possession through Court. Jinnat Ali also auction purchased the land of the entire jote for arrear of rent in Certificate case No. 214 of 1930-31 and got into possession therein and obtained sale certificate and delivery possession through Court. Elahadad Chowdhury, the father of defendant No. 21, acquired the suit land by partition with Ali and Mokbul Ali by way of a registered Ewajnama dated 27-1-33. In the meantime, Jinnat Ali filed CS No. 70 of 1929 in the Court of the Munsif at Cox''s Bazar against the heirs of Ali Hossain, Omar Ali and Ali Akbar in respect of the suit land for recovery of the khas possession in their homestead and obtained decree therein. Elahadad Chowdhury acquired 4 drones and 12 kanis of land in the suit jote by kot mortgage purchase by registered kabala from Surendra Lal Chowdhury in the benami of one Abdul Rashid. Ali Akbar, Omar Ali and the heirs of Ali Hossain thereatened Elahadad Chowdhury to redeem the kot mortgage of the said land following which Elahadad Chowdhury, Omar Ali, Ali Akbar and the heirs to Ali Hossain executed and registered a deed of Ewaj-nama. By this Ewaj-nama Ali Akbar and others relinquished their right to redeem the mortgage in favour of Ellahabad Chowdhury. The heirs of Omar Ali and Ali Akbar including their daughters and their heirs acquired 6 drones 3 kanis, 11 gondas and 1 kara of land by the solenama filed in OS No. 13 of 1951 and they relinquished their right, title, interest in the remaining petition of the suit land in favour of the heirs to Elahadad Chowdhury. It was also contended that he has been possessing 11 drones and 1 kani of land out of said Suit land, including khas land by dint of the Solenama filed in OS No. 13 of 1951. The heirs to Ali Hossain filed OS No. 13 of 1951 to which the heirs to Ali Hossain filed OS No. 35 of 1954 for cancellation of the solenama filed in OS No. 13 of 1951 but the suit was dismissed on contest and the order of dismissal of the suit was also upheld by the appellate Court. It was also contended that the plaintiffs have got no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 10. PW 1 Shafiqur Rahman, plaintiff No. 6, deposed for himself as well as for plaintiff Nos. 4-15. He stated in his evidence that the disputed land comprising 17 drones 5 kanis 1 gonda and 1 kara desor bed in the schedule to the plaint formerly belonged to Fazal Kabir Khan, who settled 14 drones of land therefrom with Md Putan, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs and some of the defendants. He stated that Md Putan acquired the suit land in the benami of his son Ali Hossain by a registered patta dated 1-2-1901 but acquired the said land with his own money and for his own benefit. He further stated that Md Putan filed OS No. 142 of 1906 against Fazal Kabir Khan, who forcibly dispossessed him from the said land, for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession therein. Eventually he obtained a decree in the suit. On appeal by Fazal Kabir Khan, the judgment of that trial Court was reversed on contest on technical grounds on the framing of the suit. Md Putan filed thereafter other suit No. 189 of 1909 against Fazal Kabir Khan for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession and obtained decree therein on contest. Against the aforesaid judgment Fazal Kabir Khan filed other appeal No. 161 of 1911 but the appeal was also dismissed on contest. He further stated that during the pendency of other appeal No. 161 of 1911 Fazal Kabir Khan transferred his rent receiving interest in said 14 drones of land to his wife Ruh Afza Kalimonnessa by a registered deed of gift. Thereafter Md Pu tan acquired the rent receiving interest of Ruh Afza in the said land by a registered kabala dated 10-6-1912 in the benami of his son, Ali Hossain with his own money and for his own benefit and Ali Hossain had no independent interest in the said land. He further stated that due to his old age Md Putan appointed Ali Hossain as his Attorney by executing a registered power of attorney in this behalf. Ali Hossain managed the suit property on behalf of his father Md Putan. The rent of the suit land fell, in arrear following which a certificate, case was started against Md Putan and Ali Hossain paid the certificate dues on behalf of Md Putan on obtaining money from one Sultan Ahmed Bahaddar by giving kot mortgage of the suit land. He further stated that Putan died in 1919 leaving Ali Hossain, Ali Akbar and Omar Ali as 3 his sons and 3 daughters named Fatema, Johara and Khodeja to succeed him. Then he gave the chain of genealogy as spelt out in the plaint. He also stated that one Makbul Ali obtained a fraudulent and collusive kabala from Fazal Kabir Khan in respect of the suit property, although Fazal Kabir Khan had already exhausted all his title and interest in the suit land by way of settlement and by way of gift to his wife Ruh Afza. One Elahadad Chowdhury acquired the right of mortgage in the suit land from Sultan Ahmed Bahaddar by a registered kabala dated 11-9-1954 and he passed the same as the mertgagee. This Makbul Ali filed a fraudulant rent suit against the heirs of Md Putan for the suit land in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong on the strengtt of his fraudulent kabala from Fazal Kabir Khan but the suit was ultimatily dismissed. The disputed land was not recorded in the RS Khatian in the name of the daughters of Md Putan, due to sheer mistake. He stated that the RS record is erroneous and is not binding upon the plaintiffs. He also sated that they have been possessing "Ka" schedule land by inhereitence theough the sons and daughters of Md Putan, He also stated that Elahadad Chowdhury failed to payment for the disputed land as mortgagee following which the disputed land was put to rent sale, which was fraudulently purchased in auction by Ellahabad Chowdhury himself in the benami of his own uncle Jinnat Ali and subsequently, in collusion with Jinnat Ali, he created a deed of partition dated 27-9-1933 to show that the disputed land fell in the exclusive share of Ellahabad Chowdhury. This was just an illegal exercise for illegally grabbing the suit property. He stated that Elahadad Chowdhury had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land on the basis of those collusive and fraudulent documents. He also stated that some of the heirs of Ali Hossain and Elahadad Chowdhury created a collusive and fraudulent deed of exchange dated 25-2-1940 in respect of the disputed land and other lands, which is void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. The wife of Ali Hossain fraudulently filed a suit for redemption of the mortgage against the heirs of Elahadad Chowdhury and in that suit a fraudulent solenama was purported to have been filed for creating a show of title in the suit land but in that suit one son and the daughters of Putan were not made parties. In terms of the aforesaid solenama the heirs of Elahadad delivered possession of 5 drones of lands in scheduled Ka to the plaint to plaintiff No. 7 in the middle part of Baishak, 1955 and since then the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land in one compact block. He stated that the plaintiffs have acquired title and interest in 6 drones 6 kara and 19 gondas of land in the suit property by inheritance through Ali Akbar, Fatema Khatun, Khodeza and Johra but they possess only 5 drones of land out of the suit land by amicable arrangement with other co-sharers. He further stated that the plaintiffs were not parties in OS No. 13 of 1951 and OS No. 35 of 1954 filed by heirs of Ali Hossain against some of heirs of Ali Hossain. He also stated that they earlier filed partition suit No. 16 of 1958 against the defendants but the said suit was dismissed as some of the co-sharers were not impleaded in the suit in time. Under such circumstances, they were constrained to file the present suit. He further stated that Jinnat Ali had never possessed the suit land by his alleged purchase in rent sale or in the mortgage sale. He also stated that Elahadad Chowdhury never possessed 11 drones 1 kani of land out of the suit land by the alleged compromise decree made in OS No. 13 of 1951. He stated that one Abdur Rahman and Abdul Sharif cultivated the share of defendant No. 5 as bargadars by executing barga kubuliyat in favour of defendant No. 5. He also stated that he filed dakhalias, one kabuliyat for the suit land but during the war of liberation the original records of the suit were destroyed along with those papers and documents. 

 17. DW 1 Nurul Islam Chowdhury, who is defendant No. 21 stated in his evidence that the disputed land formerly belonged to Fazal Kabir Khan in Jote right, who subsequently settled the same with one Ali Hussain, Ali Akbar and Md Putan in jote right, He further stated that Fazal Kabir Khan transferred his jote right in the disputed land along with other khas lands to his wife Ruh Afza by a registered deed of gift. Ruh Afza, subsequently transferred her jote right in the disputed land to Ali Hossain by a registered kabala. He stated that Md Putan did not acquire the jote right in the disputed land in the benami of his son Ali Hossain. He also stated that Md Putan, Ali Hossain and Ali Akbar transferred their jote right in suit land for 9 drones and 5 kanis of land to Tripura and Prasanna by two registered deeds of mortgage. He also stated that they transferred 4 drones and 12 kanis of land out of the disputed land to one Surendra by another registered deed of mortgage. These deeds of mortgage have been marked as Exhibits A and A(1). He stated that Tripura and Prasanna filed Mortgage Suit No. 65 of 1922 against Md Putan, Ali Hossain. and Ali Akbar for the mortgage money and the suit was decreed and the decree was put to execution and one jinnat Ali auction purchased the suit land in the mortgage execution case and got delivery of possession in the suit land through court. He further stated that Jinnat Ali filed OS No. 70 of 1929 against Md Putan, Ali Hossain and Ali Akbar for recovery of ichas possession in the homestead portion of the auction purchased land and got a decree therein and subsequently obtained delivery of possession therein through court by execution of the decree. He added that Elahadad Chowdhury purchased the mortgage interest of Surendra in the suit land in the benami of one Abdur Rashid by a registered kabala Exhibit B. He further stated that the heirs of Ali Hossain inherited their jote right in the land recorded in the RS Khatian on the strength of the kabala executed by Ruh Afza in favour of Ali Hossain. He went on to state that the Khash Mohal Estate filed certificate case on 214 of 1930-31 against the heirs of Ali Hossain for arrears of rent in respect of their joie right and got a decree therein and Jinnat Ali Chowdhury auction purchased the jote right of the heirs of Ali Hossain in the suit land and got delivery of possession. He further stated that Elahadad Chowdhury acquired the suit land by a deed of partition in the form of a deed of exchange in 1933 from Jinnat Ali. Makbul Ali and Gura Meah. The deed of partition has been marked as Exhibit E. He further stated that a deed of exchange was also executed and registered between Elahadad Chowdhury and the heirs of Ali Akbar, Ali Hossain, Omar Ali and others in the disputed land. The deed of exchange has been marked as Exhibit F by which the heirs of Ali Akbar, Ali Hossain and Omar Ali acquired 3 drones 11 kanis and 11 gondas in the suit land. He further stated that Mehernessa a daughter of Ali Hossain filed OS No. 13 of 1951 against the heirs of Elahadad Chowdhury for redemption of kot mortgage of the suit land and the suit was decreed compromise in terms of a solenama. The heirs of Ali Hossain. Ali Akbar and Omar Ali were parties in OS No. 13 of 1951. He also signed the solenama. He stated that the heirs of Ali Hossain, Ali Akbar and Omar Ali got 6 drones 3 kanis 11 gondas 1 kara of land out of the disputed land while the heirs of Elahadad Chowdhury got 11 drones and 1 kani of land. He further stated that they possess 11 drones and 1 kani of land in the suit. He also stated that the kot mortgage land of Surendra was subsequently purchased by Elahadad Chowdhury and the same fell in the saham of the heirs Ali Hossain, Ali Akbar and Omar Ali by Solenama filed in OS No. 13 of 1951. He stated that the heirs of Ali Hossain filed OS No. 35 of 1954 against the heirs of Elahadad Chowdhury and others for cancellation of the solenama filed in OS No. 13 of 1951 and for redemption of kot mortgage of Sultan Ahmed Bahaddar and for setting aside the deed of Exchange Exhibit F which was dismissed on contest by the trial Court, and the said judgment was eventually affirmed by the High Court and the Supreme Court. He also stated that the names of the heirs of Ali Hossain, Ali Akbar and Omar Ali have been correctly recorded in the RS and BS Khatians in respect of 6 drones 3 kanis 11 gondas and 1 kara of the disputed land. The kot mortgage right of Sultan Ahmed Bahaddar has been declared as void and illegal in OS Suit No. 13 of 1951 and 35 of 1954 and as such the plaintiffs are not entitled to get any share in the disputed land on partition and the plaintiffs are not their co-sharer in respect of 11 drones and 1 kani of land, and they have no title and possession therein. 

 26. Now coming to the documentary evidence adduced by the contending parties in support of their respective claims of title and possession we are to consider how far the contending parties have been able to substantiate their claims with reference to the exhibited documents. The case of the plaintiffs is that the suit land comprising 17 drones 5 kanis 1 gonda and 1 kara as fully described in schedule Ka'' to the plaint formerly belonged to Fazal Kabir Khan who possessed the same in khas. In course of time, the said Fazal Kabir Khan settled 14 drones of land with Md Putan, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs and some of the defendants, by a registered patta dated 1-2-1919 in the benami of his son Ali Hossain, who owned and possessed the same. Thereafter, Fazal Kabir Khan transferred the said 14 drones of land along with other 3 drones 5 kanis 1 gonda 1 kara of land to his wife Ruh Afza by a registered deed of gift whereby he transferred the rent receiving interest to his wife in the 14 drones of land and the jote right in 3 drones 5 kanis and 1 kara of land. The said Ruh Afza thereafter sold her entire interests of the suit property to Md Putan by registered kabalas. Although this land was acquired by registered kabala by Md Putan in the benami of his son Ali Hossain, the latter was simply a name lender and Md Putan owned and possesAd the disputed land in his own right and for his own benefit. The contention of defendant No. 21, on the other hand, is that Md Putan and Ali Hossain jointly acquired 14 drones of the land out of the suit land from Fazal Kabir Khan by way of settlement by a registered patta dated 1-2-1901 by which they acquired the rent receiving interest in the said land and khash interest in 3 drones 5 kanis, 1 kara and 1 gonda of land by purchase from Ruh Afza, wife of Fazal Kabir Khan. The plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 1-18, 20 and 30 are the heirs and sons and daughters of Md Putan. The contending defendant No. 21 admitted that Md Putan acquired 14 drones of land in the suit land by way of settlement from Fazal Kabir Khan in Dar Jote right by a registered patta. Md Putan also acquired the rent receiving interest in the said 14 drones of land and jote interest in only 3 drones 5 kanis 1 gonda and 1 kara by way of purchase by a registered kabala from Ruh Afza in the benami of his son Ali Hossain. The plaintiff''s, witnesses uniformly stated that Ali Hossain was simply a benamder in respect of the suit land covered by registered patta dated 1-10-1921 and by registered sale deed from Ruh Afza, wife of Fazal Kabir Khan. On detailed consideration of the evidence on record, both oral and documentary, the learned Subordinate Judge found that except the solitary and uncorroborated statements of DW 1 there is no other evidence on record to prove that Ali Hossain and Ali Akbar acquired the Dar Jote right in the suit land along with their father Md Putan by settlement from Fazal Kabir Khan on the basis of registered patta dated 1-2-1901. The contesting defendant also failed to prove that Ali Akbar, Ali Hossain and Omar Ali acquired the jote right in the suit land by purchase from Ruh Afza, wife of Fazal Kabir Khan with their own money and for their own benefit and that with the income of the said property. On proper appreciation of the evidence on record the learned Subordinate Judge came to the firm finding that Md Putan acquired the jote right in the suit land by way of settlement from Fazal Kabir Khan by registered patta dated 1-2-1921 as well as by way of registered kabalas from Ruh Afza, who had earlier acquired the said land by way of gift from her husband Fazal Kabir Khan by a registered instrument. The learned Subordinate Judge also found that Md Putan acquired 16 annas interest in the suit land in Dar Jote right as well as in jote right. 

 27. The main contention between the contending parties appears to be entering around the question as to whether Md Putan acquired the suit property in 14 drones with his own money and for his own benefit and Ali Hossain was simply his benamder and a constituted attorney or the said property was actually acquired by Ali Hossain with his own money and for his own benefit. Ali Hossain, of course kot mortgaged the said land with Sultan Ahmed Bahaddar for payment of rent of the suit land to the landlords. Subsequently, the said Sultan Ahmed sold his mortgage right in the suit land to Elahadad Chowdhury but thereafter the said mortgage was redeemed amicably. This has been contended by the contesting defendant that Md Putan and Ali Hossain transferred 9 drone 4 kani of land from the suit property to Tripura and Prosanna by kot mortgage, who subsequently filed Mortgage Suit No. 25 of 1921 for realisation mortgage money and got a preliminary decree therein and in execution of the mortgage decree their mortgage interest was sold to Jinnat Ali. In this way Jinnat Ali purchased the decree of the mortgage suit, being Mortgage suit No. 61 of 1921, from Tripura and Prassana. The sale certificate has been marked as Exhibit C(1) and the corresponding writ of delivery of possession has been marked as Exhibit D(1), but which Jinnat Ali is alleged to have purchased the suit land in auction on 12-5-1925 in Mortgage Execution case No. 14 of 1925 filed by Tripura and by Tripura and Prassana against the heirs of Ali Hussain and some of the heirs of Md Putan. The certificate case No. 214 of 1930-31 was instituted by the Khas Mahal Estate for arrears of land revenue against the heirs of Ali Hossain and Elahadad Chowdhury, following which Jinnat Ali purchased the suit property in the aforesaid certificate case. Defendant No. 21 contends that his father Elahadad Chowdhury acquired the suit land on partition by a registered deed of partition dated 27-9-1933 Exhibit E concluded between Elahadad Chowdhury, Jinnat Ali and others. There is nothing on record to show that Elahadad acquired any interest in the suit land before 27-9-1933 and as such Exhibit E is merely a paper transaction. The name of the Elahadad Chowdhury was recorded in the RS Khatian as a mortgage. The RS Khatian has been marked Exhibit 2 and Elahadad Chowdhury is the certificate debtor in certificate case No. 214 of 1930-31, but Tripura, Prassana and Jinnat Ali were not the certificate debtors in the certificate case. From all these the learned Subordinate Judge concluded that Elahadad Chowdhury acquired only kot mortgage right in the suit jote from Sultan Ahmed Bahaddar, who had acquired the same from Ali Hossain and Putan in only kot mortgage right and consequently the sale certificate Exhibit C the RS Khatian Exhibit 2, Kabala Exhibit 6 clearly falsify the case of defendant No. 21 that Ali Hossain and Md Putan transferred the suit land to Prassana and Tripura. Moreover, it appears from the record that Md Putan and his heirs and heiresses were not certificate debtors in certificate case No. 214 of 1930-31, although defendant No. 21 admitted that Md Putan had one third share in the disputed jote. It is also found that only the heirs of Ali Hossain and Elahadad Chowdhury were made parties in Certificate case No. 214 of 1930-31. On consideration of all these documents the alleged sale of the suit land to Jinnat Ali in Certificate case No. 214 of 1930-31 vide Exhibit C has been found by the learned Subordinate Judge as fraudulent, oollusive and void as a result of which Jinnat Ali acquired no interest in the suit land against Ali Hossain and Elahadad Chowdhury. The contention of the plaintiffs that Md Putan transferred the suit land to one Sultan Ahmed Bahaddar by a registered kot mortgage deed in mortgage right, who subsequently sold the said mortgage right to Elahadad Chowdhury, father of the appellant, acquired only the kot mortgage interest of Md Putan in the suit land by registered kabala dated 9-7-1926 (Exhibit 6 this kabala Exhibit 6) and the RS Khatian Exhibit 3 clearly prove that Md Putan transferred the suit land to Sultan Ahmed Bahaddar in kot mortgage right and Elahadad Chowdhury, purchased the said right of Sultan Ahmed by registered kabala Exhibit 6 and as such his mane was recorded in the RS Khatian as a mortgagee. It is also found from the record that the Khas Mohal Estate filed certified case No. 214 of 1930-31 against Elahadad Chowdhury for realisation of arrear of rent in respect of the suit land Exhibit C but the names of Tripura, Prassana and Surrendra and Jinnat Ali, Abdur Rashid do not appear in the RS Khatian as mortgagee and they were not parties in certificate case No. 214 of 1930-31, while Elahadad Chowdhury alone was a party in the suit certificate case. The basis of the claim of the appellant is that Elahadad Chowdhury acquired right, title, interest and possession in the suit land by deed of partition dated 27-9-1933 with Jinnat Ali and others, in which Elahadad Chowdhury had no title whatsoever, this deed of partition Exhibit E has rightly been found to be a fraudulent and collusive one, created for the purpose of the suit. 

 29. The learned Subordinate Judge also found that Surrendra, Prassanna and Tripura never possessed the suit property as mortgagees and the alleged mortgage decree in Mortgage suit No. 65 of 1921 is collusive and fraudulent. The learned trial Court further found that the kot mortgage deed Exhibit A -and A(1), kabala Exhibit B and the sale certificate Exhibit C(1) and the writ of delivery of possession Exhibit D(1) are all collusive and fraudulent paper transactions and these were never acted upon. This findings are based on evidence on record and are well reasoned. From those the learned trial Court found that the purchase of the suit land in auction by Jinnat Ali in Certificate case No. 214 of 1930-31 vide Exhibit C is out and out a fraudulent exercise and he never possessed the suit land. The learned trial Court also found that kabala Exhibit 6 the RS Khatian Exhibit 2 made it manifestly clear that Elahadad Chowdhury acquired only the mortgage right in the suit land from Sultan Ahmed Bahaddar, who had acquired the same from Md Putan through his Attorney Ali Hossain. The plaintiff and defendant Nos. 1-18, 20-30 contended that Elahadad Chowdhury acquired the suit land in kot mortgage right by way of purchase from Sultan Ahmed Bahaddar by kabala Exhibit 6 but subsequently he fraudulently purchased the suit land in auction in certificate case No. 214 of 1930-31 in the benami of his uncle Jinnat Ali and thereafter collusively created deed of partition Exhibit E with Jinnat Ali which is out and out a fraudulent transaction. This finding of the trial Court is also well supported by the evidence on record, both oral and documentary. The learned Subordinate Judge further found that the certificate sale of the suit land in certificate case No. 214 of 1930-31 was collusive, fraudulent and void sale which did not in any way affect the right, further interest and possession of the heirs of Md Putan, particularly his 3 daughters namely Khodeja, Fatema and Jahura, and consequently Jinnat Ali acquired no-interest in the suit property by the aforesaid sale. The contesting defendant filed the certified copy of an Ewaznama dated 26-12-1940. Exhibit F, which purports to show that Ali Akbar, Omar Ali and Ali Hossain acquired 3 drones 1 kanis 11 gondas out of the suit land from Elahadad by this deed of Ewaznaina. It has been stated in paragraph 19 of the written statement by defendant No. 21 that Jinnat Ali filed other suit No. 20 of 1929 in the court of Munsif at Cox''s Bazar for.recovery of the khas possession in the suit land on the strength of the alleged purchase in Mortgage suit.No. 14 of 1925 against Ali Akbar, Omar Ali and heirs of Ali Hossain and the said suit was decreed. It was further stated that Ali Akbar and the heirs of Ali Hossain amicably redeemed the mortgage of the suit land from Elahadad Chowdhury executing an Ewaznama Exhibit F by which Ali Akbar, Omar Ali and some other heirs of Md Putan got 3 drones 11 kanis and 11 gondas of land while Elahadad Chowdhury got the remaining portion of the suit property. But in this Ewaznama Exhibit F the three daughters of Md Putan named Khodeja, Fatema and Johura were not parties and as such the same is never binding upon them although the same is binding upon the parties thereto. It is thus evident that the right, title, interest and possession of plaintiffs Nos. 4-15 and defendant No. 7 and 11, the heirs and heiresses of Khatija. Fatema and Johura. The three daughters of Md Putan, remained totally unaffected by the alleged purchase of the suit land by Jinnat Ali, uncle of Elahadad Chowdhury, in mortgage Execution case No. 14 of 1925, by the alleged certificate purchase of Jinnat Ali in certificate case No. 214 of 1930-31, by the alleged partition deed Exhibit F between Jinnat Ali and Elahadad Chowdhury and by the so called Ewaznama deed Exhibit F. It is also found that the compromise decree dated 26-11-52 Exhibit H obtained in 0 S No. 13 of 1951 filed by Moherunnessa daughter of Ali Akbar, against defendant No. 21 and others for redemption of the kot mortgage right in the suit land did not at all affect the interest of the heirs and heiresses of Khodeja, Fatema and Johura, 3 daughters of Md Putan as they were not made parties to the said suit but the said compromise decree dated 16-9-42 in OS No. 13 of 1951 is binding upon the heirs of Ali Hossain, Ali Akbar and Omar Ali. Thus the interest of plaintiffs Nos. 4-15 and defendants 7 and 11 remained totally intact to the extent of 3rd share in the suit property. It is also found that by the compromise decree Exhibit H defendant No. 21 and other heirs of Elahadad Chowdhury became co-sharers in the suit land. 

 31. Mr Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant submits that since defendant No. 21 is a stranger to the suit land and his possession therein has been admitted by the plaintiffs themselves, a simple suit for partition without a prayer for declaration of title and confirmation of possession and for recovery of khas possession is not maintainable in law. In support of his contention, Mr Karim has referred to the case of Gagan Chandra Hazra and another vs Surendra Nath Khamral and others reported in AIR 1951 Calcutta 410. The cited decision is obviously of no assistance to the appellant as we have already found that Elahadad Chowdhury is not a stranger to the suit jote but a co-sharer thereto on the basis of the decree obtained in 0 S No. 13 of 1951. Exhibit H. This case has a chequered career starting from 1910 when Fazal Karim Khan settled the suit land with Mr Putan by registered patta dated 2nd Falgoon. 1308 BS. Soon thereafter the said landlords dispossessed Md Putan form the suit land which necessitated the filing of Title Suit No. 142 of 1906 by Putan against Fazal Karim Khan for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. The said suit was eventually decreed on contest on 18-3-1907. The appeal by Fazal Karim Khan against the aforesaid judgment and decree in favour of Md Putan was allowed due to some formal defects in the plaint. Thereafter Md Putan filed title suit No. 89 of 1908 against Fazal Karim Khan as a principal defendant and Ali Hossain, his son, as a pro-forma defendant, for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in the suit land and the said suit was decreed on 23-1-1911. Title appeal No. 101 of 1911 filed by Fazal Karim Khan against the aforesaid decree was dismissed on contest and right, title and interest of Md Putan was confirmed. In the mean time Fazal Karim Khan transferred his superior interest in 14 drones of the suit land and khas interest in 3 drones 5 kanis 1 gonda and 1 kara of land, out of the suit land, to his wife Ruh Afza alias Alimannessa by a registered deed of gift dated 18th Magh, 1316 BS. Thereafter Ruh Afza transferred her superior interest in 14 drones of the suit land and khas interest in 3 drones 5 kanis 1 gonda and 1 kara of land to Md Putan by registered kabala dated 10-6-1912 Mr Putan acquired the suit property in the benami of his son Ali Hossain but it was acquired with his own money and for his own benefit and Ali Hossain as simply a namlender, have no interest of his own therein. Due to his old age Md Putan appointed his son Ali Hossain as his constituted attorney for the management of the suit property as he himself could not look after the same due to physical infirmity. In course of time, Ali Hossain kot mortgaged the suit property with one Sultan Ahmed Bahaddar on behalf of his father Md Putan for saving the suit property from auction sale initiated for arrears of land revenue. Md Putan died in 1919 leaving his son Ali Hossain, Omar Ali, and Ali Akbar as his 3 sons and Khodeja, Johura and Fatema as his three daughters to succeed him. Defendant Nos. 1-6, 8-10, 12-19 and 20, 30 are the heirs and heiresses of the aforesaid 3 sons of Md Putan while plaintiff Nos. 4-15 and defendants 7 and 11 are the heirs and heiresses of Khodeja, Johura and Fatema, 3 daughters of Md Putan and they own and posses the suit property in ejmali. Md Fazal Kabir Khan and his heirs having greedy eyes over the suit property nevertheless undertook numerous abortive attempts and made unrelenting efforts and resorted to various exercises for laying claim upon the suit property by setting up their relation. Jinnat Ali and others. Fazal Karim Khan purchased the kot mortgage right in the suit property in Mortgage suit No. 25 of 1921 in the benami of Jinnat Ali in Mortgage Execution case No. 14 of 1925, certificate case No. 214 of 1930-31 was instituted by the Khas Mahal Estate for arrears of land revenue against Ali Hossain and the suit property was purchased by Jinnat Ali. Thereafter Elahadad Chowdhury created partition deed dated 27-9-1933 Exhibit E'' in collusion with uncle Jinnat Ali and others, although he had no interest in the suit land. This Exhibit E'' is evidently a paper transaction designed to create false show of interest in the suit property in favour of Fazal Kabir Khan. The learned trial Court rightly found that Elahadad Chowdhury acquired only kot mortgage right in the suit jote from Sultan Ahmed Bahaddar and nothing more than that. This auction sale in question has clearly been found to be fraudulent and collusive as the heirs and heiresses of Md Putan were not made parties as certificate debtors in certificate case No. 214 of 1931, although admittedly Md Putan had one third share in the suit Jote. Inspite of all these exercises by Fazal Kabir Khan, and Elahadad Chowdhury, the heirs and heiresses of Md Putan have been able to successfully withstand their onslaughts and managed to hold on to the suit land in assertion of their own title and interest. Fazal Kabir Khan and his successor want to the extent of entering into special deals with some of the heirs and heiresses of Ali Hossain and his heirs in their bid to dislodge the plaintiff from their unassailable position. In the facts and circumstances in the case and the evidence on record, we are satisfied that the plaintiffs have been able to prove their case by cogent and reliable evidence and the learned Subordinate Judge rightly decreed the suit on proper appreciation of the evidence on record. We do not find any justifiable ground to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree which are well reasoned and well supported by the evidence, we do not thereafter find any substance in the appeal. The impugned judgment is found to be based on proper appreciation of the evidence on record and correct principle of law. The submission made by the learned Advocate for the appellants are consequently found to be of substance and the same are accordingly repelled.
